insight.title: How Light Paints the World
insight.subtitle: The quiet dialogue between the sun and our eyes.

sections.text: Every morning, the world emerges from a deep, velvet shadow. We wake to a room filled with color, yet color does not live inside the objects themselves. Instead, it is a fleeting gift from the sun. Without the gentle touch of traveling beams, the red apple and the blue sea are exactly the same.

Science tells us that light travels in tiny, silent waves. When these waves strike a surface, the object keeps some for itself and reflects others back to us. Your eyes catch these wandering rays, turning them into a signal. In that instant, your mind builds a vibrant map of the space around you.

This means you never truly touch the world with your hands alone. You perceive it through a constant, shimmering rain of energy. It is a reminder that we are deeply connected to the stars. We are not just observers of the light; we are the very place where the universe finally sees itself.

news.title: The ‘3-hour dinner rule’: Doctors say this simple change could improve heart health and longevity

news.title: DNA origami vaccine platform shows promise against multiple infectious viruses
news.description: The COVID-19 pandemic brought messenger RNA (mRNA) vaccines to the forefront of global health care. After their clinical trial stages, the first COVID-19 mRNA vaccine was administered on 8 December 2020 and mathematical models suggest that mRNA vaccines prevented at least 14.4 million deaths from COVID-19 in the first year alone.
